title: Introspection Illusion
coreMove: Test the appearance created by introspection, then replace it with a visible check on reality.
sourcePressure: The frozen TOC and official source notes frame Introspection Illusion as a specific decision error around introspection, shallow thinking, verbal reports. Traceable support includes Shallow Thoughts About the Self: The Automatic Components of Self-Assessment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating Introspection Illusion as generic advice to be smarter, instead of forcing this exact move: test the appearance created by introspection, then replace it with a visible check on reality.

hook: Do not open with a definition of Introspection Illusion.
Do not use a generic panic-at-a-meeting opener.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable shape where the obvious answer is wrong and the opposite is true.
Do not make Introspection Illusion sound like ordinary carelessness.
examples: No coffee mug, classroom whiteboard, bus depot, radiator, bike helmet, or narrow kitchen shell.
No example may skip the specific mechanics of Introspection Illusion.
